correctness.rationale: Pinned RESULT.md and check_exact.py inspected. The Laurent–Nogueira horizontal rational-tongue bounds are explicitly credited. Coprime upper and lower mechanical binary words have cyclic prefix-sum discrepancies in {0,1}; summation by parts locates the q-cycle coordinates strictly inside (0,1) except a single zero/one contact. Differentiating their actual periodic recurrences at fixed hitting coordinate yields L′(λ),U′(λ)=−sum_j λ^(q−1−j)x_j/Q_q<0, ensuring globally unique inverse endpoints. Coprime floor sums S(1)=p and S′(1)=(p−1)(q−1)/2 yield L′(1)=−(q−1)/(2q) and U′(1)=−(q+1)/(2q). Independent rational Fraction calculation checked 597 (p,q,λ) configurations q≤25 including derivative signs and boundary width coefficients. Finite check does not replace arbitrary coprime p,q proof.

value.rationale: The geometry of rational mode-locking tongues is a natural bifurcation object; global inversion makes a previously implicit vertical slice exact and the denominator-only sharp wedge coefficient identifies universal arithmetic scaling at each rational vertex. This is not routine substitution because nonfolding of the boundary functions needs a nontrivial cyclic mechanical-word argument.

final_claim: For reduced 0<p<q and fixed 0<b<1, the p/q rational tongue of R_{λ,b}(x)={λx+b} is empty when b≤p/q and otherwise a single closed interval of λ∈(0,1); endpoints uniquely invert known polynomial boundary functions and the near-(p/q,1) width has numerator-independent coefficient 4q/(q²-1).
